flashcard_questions.q: What is an embedded system in computing?
flashcard_questions.a: A computer built into a larger device to carry out one dedicated function.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a microcontroller inside an embedded system?
flashcard_questions.a: A single chip that combines a processor with memory and input/output connections.

flashcard_questions.q: What is firmware in an embedded system?
flashcard_questions.a: The permanent program that controls the device, usually stored in read-only memory.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is firmware normally stored in read-only memory?
flashcard_questions.a: So it is ready the instant the device is switched on.

flashcard_questions.q: How does firmware differ from ordinary software on a laptop?
flashcard_questions.a: Firmware is written once for the device and normally stays the same for its life.
A system that must respond to its inputs immediately, without any noticeable delay.

flashcard_questions.q: Which car safety feature is given as a real-time embedded example?
Why do designers give an embedded system only just enough processing power?
flashcard_questions.a: A bigger processor would only waste money and energy.
A computer designed to run many different programs, such as a laptop or smartphone.

flashcard_questions.q: How is the function of an embedded system decided?
flashcard_questions.a: It is fixed when the device is manufactured and cannot easily be changed.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is an embedded system cheaper to make than a full computer?
flashcard_questions.a: The hardware only does one job, so it can be smaller and simpler.

flashcard_questions.q: Name an embedded system found in a kitchen appliance.
Which medical device is named as an embedded system?
Why must an embedded system such as a pacemaker be highly reliable?
flashcard_questions.a: It must work perfectly every time, so its hardware and firmware are kept simple.
